title: Who Wrote the OU Chant? Jessie Lone Clarkson Gilkey's 1936 Alma Mater
question: Who wrote the OU Chant and when was it written?
answer: The OU Chant, Oklahoma's alma mater, was written in 1936 by Jessie Lone Clarkson Gilkey, who directed the university's girls' glee club from 1936 to 1938. Fans traditionally raise one index finger while it plays.
summary: The OU Chant was written in 1936 by glee club director Jessie Lone Clarkson Gilkey. Learn the history of OU's alma mater and the raised-finger tradition.
body: Before the Sooners take the field at home, the noise in Norman briefly turns reverent. The Pride of Oklahoma plays the OU Chant, the university's alma mater, and the crowd sings along. It is a softer moment than "Boomer Sooner," and for many fans it is the most emotional part of game day.

The chant was written in 1936 by Jessie Lone Clarkson Gilkey, who directed OU's girls' glee club from 1936 to 1938. She made a quick impression on campus, and in 1937 she was voted Outstanding Faculty Woman. Her song became the university's alma mater and has outlasted generations of coaches, players and students.

The words are easy to recognize. The chant opens by spelling out O-K-L-A-H-O-M-A and goes on to praise a campus beautiful by day and night, with colors gleaming red and white under a western sky. It joined an even older piece of OU spirit: back in 1895, the year of OU's first football game, students adopted a yell built around Boomer Sooner and Okla-U.

The chant comes with its own gesture. Fans, students, athletes and alumni are encouraged to raise one finger in the air while it plays, a sign of the university's greatness and the unity of all Sooners. Today the song is performed during pregame at home football games and at other official university gatherings, which keeps a 1930s glee club song very much alive.
